what_its_for: This ear drop medicine is used to treat bacterial infections of the outer ear canal (also called swimmer's ear or otitis externa). It contains two antibiotics (neomycin and colistin) to fight the infection, a steroid (hydrocortisone) to reduce swelling, redness, and pain, and thonzonium which helps the medicine work better inside the ear.
how_to_take: Use this medicine only in the ear — never in the eye or by mouth. Shake the bottle well before each use. Lie down or tilt your head so the infected ear faces up. Gently pull the earlobe up and back (for adults) or down and back (for children) to straighten the ear canal. Carefully squeeze the prescribed number of drops into the ear. Stay in this position for at least 5 minutes so the drops can reach deep into the ear canal. You may place a small cotton plug loosely in the ear afterward if your doctor recommends it. Wash your hands before and after using.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 4 drops placed into the affected ear 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor may adjust this based on your condition. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions. Do not use more drops or use it more often than directed. Treatment is usually for 10 days or less.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep out of reach of children. Throw away any unused medicine after your treatment is finished or after the expiration date on the label — do not save it for later use.
what_to_avoid: Do not use this medicine in your eyes. Do not put the dropper tip directly into your ear, as this can contaminate the bottle. Avoid getting water in the treated ear while swimming or bathing — your doctor may ask you to keep that ear dry during treatment. Do not use this medicine if your eardrum is perforated (has a hole) unless your doctor specifically tells you it is safe to do so. Do not use longer than prescribed, as overuse can lead to resistant infections or fungal overgrowth in the ear.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: a skin rash, itching, hives, or signs of an allergic reaction; increased redness, swelling, or pain in or around the ear; no improvement after a few days of treatment or if symptoms get worse; any dizziness, ringing in the ears, or hearing changes; if you accidentally get the drops in your eyes or swallow any of the medicine.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in pain and discomfort within the first 1 to 2 days of treatment. However, it is very important to continue using all doses for the full course your doctor prescribed, even if your ear feels better sooner. Stopping too early may allow the infection to come back.
special_populations: Children: This medicine can be used in children, but use extra care when administering the drops. Pull the earlobe down and back for young children to straighten the ear canal. Elderly: No special dose changes are typically needed, but use with caution. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Perforated Eardrum: Do NOT use this medicine if you have a hole in your eardrum unless your doctor has confirmed it is safe — the antibiotic ingredients can potentially cause hearing damage if they reach the middle ear.
